name: ping-pong-loop
title: Ping-pong loading loop
summary: A syncing card with two endless loops from continuousSec(): a puck that glides back and forth along a track (a triangle wave eased with smooth_step) and three dots that bounce in turn (phase-shifted sines).
prompt: A 'Syncing photos' card with a looping progress animation: a glowing puck sliding back and forth along a track, slowing at each end, and three bouncing dots under it.
teaches: Turn a clock into a 0→1→0 ping-pong with abs((continuousSec() / 1.5) % 2 - 1) and soften the ends with smooth_step(x, 1, 0)
Stagger a loop by phase: sin(continuousSec() * 7.5 - i * 0.9) inside a loop gives each dot its own beat, and max(0, …) keeps only the hop
Use continuousSec() for endless motion: it is what schedules the repaint
pitfalls: smooth_step takes (value, max, min): smooth_step(x, 1, 0) is the usual smoothstep(0, 1, x)
continuousSec() repaints every frame for as long as the document is shown: fine for a loading state, wasteful for a static card (DX-05)
The render tool's clock has whole-second resolution: pin a clock such as 10:00:01 to get a mid-swing frame
Scale the travel with componentWidth(): a literal 280 dp swing on a 336 dp track stops short on a wide host and runs off a narrow one

snippets.note: swing = abs((continuousSec() / 1.5) % 2 - 1): a 3 s triangle wave
px = 40 + (componentWidth() - 80) * smooth_step(@swing, 1, 0): eased at both ends, across whatever width the canvas gets
three dots hopping with phase-shifted sines

check.describe: At 10:00:01 the puck is about a quarter along the track, moving left, and the first dot is up with the others lower; at 10:00:00 the puck is at the right end. Resized (narrow 240, wide 540) the track spans the canvas less 24 dp each side, the puck swings across all of it and the dots stay centred.
